claim_boundary: Coin Metrics defines AdrBalCnt as the count of unique addresses with a positive native-unit balance and describes address metrics as a proxy for network users. It also warns that one user can control many addresses and custodial addresses can represent many users. The source does not establish that four-week address-count growth predicts BTC returns or supports a profitable long-or-cash policy.

independence_and_duplicate_boundary.distinct_mechanism: This family measures the stock of funded addresses, not the closed daily active-address and transaction-count activity flow. A funded address can remain counted without current transaction activity.
independence_and_duplicate_boundary.closed_onchain_activity_boundary: Do not reintroduce AdrActCnt, TxCnt, their breadth conjunction, annual comparison, DRA admission parent or any outcome-aware combination from the closed activity families.
independence_and_duplicate_boundary.prohibited_rescue: Do not add wallet clustering, address-balance thresholds, USD thresholds, active addresses, transaction counts, price normalization, alternate lags or smoothing after source or outcome access.

adversarial_prior: A Bitcoin user can control many addresses, while an exchange or custodian address can represent many users.
UTXO wallet change-address and privacy behavior can increase funded-address count without economic adoption.
Dusting, consolidation and wallet software changes can create or remove addresses independently of investment demand.
The funded-address stock may trend upward so strongly that the nonexpansion state is too sparse for a valid test.
Present-vintage historical data lacks original daily publication and revision vintages; any historical pass remains discovery only.
